title: Non-Differentiability of Absolute Value at a Corner
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Show that f(x) = |x - 3| is continuous at x = 3, but fails to be differentiable at x = 3.
finalAnswer: f \text{ is continuous at } x = 3, \text{ but } f'(3) \text{ does not exist because } f'_+(3) = 1 \neq -1 = f'_-(3)

steps.title: Verify Continuity at x = 3
steps.explanation: Direct substitution demonstrates that the limit equals the function value.

steps.title: Conclude Failure of Differentiability
steps.explanation: The two one-sided derivatives disagree, creating a sharp corner.
steps.why: A derivative exists if and only if both one-sided derivatives agree.
